title: SL(2,3) counting is polynomial with bounded homology
claim: Target: let G be a finite group with a central elementary abelian 2-subgroup A of rank m, a normal subgroup N containing A with N/A elementary abelian, and G/N nilpotent. For a finite presentation P = <X | R> let E be the exponent-sum matrix mod 2 and k the dimension of its left kernel (k = dim H^2 of the presentation complex with F2 coefficients). Then |Hom(P, G)| = |Hom(P, A)| times the sum over homomorphisms psi: P -> G/N of the number of points v of the affine space of twisted lifts of psi to G/A (solutions of linear equations over F2) at which the lifting obstruction vanishes. With generator lifts s(psi(x)) n~(v_x), the A-valued sign of every relator is a polynomial of degree at most 2 in the F2-coordinates of v (the central extension A -> N -> N/A has a bilinear cocycle, conjugation by coset representatives adds quadratic corrections, inverses add squares), and a lift exists exactly when the vector of signs lies in the image of E, that is, when m k quadratic forms vanish; Gauss sums over F2 count these zeros. Hence for fixed G and a fixed bound on dim H^1(P; F_p) for the primes p dividing |G/N| and on k, |Hom(P, G)| is computable in polynomial time. Balanced presentations of closed orientable 3-manifold groups (Heegaard diagrams, integral surgery on knot diagrams) with bounded first homology satisfy the bounds. SL(2,3) satisfies the hypotheses with A = {I, -I}, N = Q8, G/N = Z3, but is not abelian-by-nilpotent; so with bounded homology the polynomial side strictly contains the abelian-by-nilpotent groups, and with S4 hard the line is not abelian-by-nilpotent.
failure_conditions: A presentation on which the algorithm and brute-force enumeration disagree.
A relator sign that is not a polynomial of degree at most 2 in the lift coordinates, or a Gauss-sum evaluation that disagrees with brute force.
A failure of the structural claims: SL(2,3) has A = {I,-I} central, N = Q8 with N/A elementary abelian and G/N = Z3, and no abelian normal subgroup with nilpotent quotient.
A control that cannot fail: dropping the obstruction must overcount on some closed manifold, and S4 must admit no such structure.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite presentations, with polynomial time when the mod-p first homology (p dividing |G/N|) and the mod-2 second homology of the presentation complex are bounded; this covers balanced presentations of closed orientable 3-manifold groups with bounded first homology. Cited, not proved: polynomial-time Gauss sums of quadratic forms over F2 (standard; Samperton-Weiss Lemma 3.1.2), and the enumeration of maps to a nilpotent quotient (BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001B). Not covered: central layers with nontrivial action or of odd exponent, and higher nilpotency class in N. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof (cited: polynomial-time Gauss sums of quadratic polynomials over F2, the affine lifting and nilpotent-quotient steps of BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001B, conversion of triangulations to balanced presentations); check.py (standard library, about 1 s) verifies the structure of SL(2,3) (normal subgroups 1, 2, 8, 24; not abelian-by-nilpotent; Fitting height 2) and that S4 admits no such structure, Gauss sums against brute force on 400 random quadratics, the algorithm against brute force on 240 cases (four groups: SL(2,3), Q8, D8, Z2 x SL(2,3); 35 integral surgeries on five knots and 25 random presentations each) with the degree-2 property of every relator sign tested at random points, a scale run up to lift spaces of dimension 26, and controls (dropping the obstruction overcounts where H^2(M;F2) is nonzero). No human or external review
